aria: Animated recap of the Wizards' 103 to 99 win over the Raptors: Kyshawn George's 27-foot 3-pointer with 8:55 left that capped an 11-0 run, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Anthony Davis' 25 points and 14 rebounds, the top scorers, how the Wizards won, and Friday's game in Chicago.
notes: Box score from the Wizards' 103–99 win over the Toronto Raptors at Scotiabank Arena on Nov 18, 2026, from the Covers box score and team stats, checked against the FOX Sports game page, with game details from The Canadian Press (via TSN and The Globe and Mail), Field Level Media and the AP/Canadian Press story on Yahoo Sports. All 103 Washington points and all 99 Toronto points are accounted for in the Covers player lines, and the quarter scores add up to both totals: Washington 29–23 after one, 49–47 at the half, Toronto 79–78 after three, Washington 25–20 in the fourth. Team stats (free throws 20 of 27 to 7 of 14, rebounds 51–41, blocks 7–3, fast-break points 12–9, points in the paint 38–46, biggest leads Washington 10, Toronto 3) are from Covers. Sources differ on Toronto's turnovers (7 or 8), so they are left out. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Wednesday's games.

Washington trailed 82–80 early in the fourth before Alex Sarr's dunk started an 11–0 run that Kyshawn George capped with a 3-pointer at 8:55 (Field Level Media; The Canadian Press). Trae Young's free throw made it 98–88 with 3:48 left (Field Level Media). Toronto got within 102–99, Jamison Battle missed a 3 with three seconds left, and Anthony Davis made one of two free throws (Field Level Media). AJ Dybantsa's 23 points and 12 rebounds were career highs, his first NBA double-double (Field Level Media; SB Nation via Yahoo Sports). The win ended Washington's eight-game losing streak; Toronto has lost six straight (AP/Canadian Press). Toronto played without Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes and RJ Barrett (AP/Canadian Press). Washington plays at Chicago on Friday (AP/Canadian Press).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Kyshawn George's 27-foot 3-pointer with 8:55 left that gave Washington a 91–82 lead, capping an 11–0 run (The Canadian Press gives the distance, clock and score; Field Level Media confirms the run, the clock and the score). The recaps don't describe the shot further, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from beyond the arc. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Washington Wizards or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to George's listed 6-foot-8 and 200 pounds (Wikipedia), with his arms scaled to the 6-foot-10¼ wingspan measured at the 2024 NBA Draft Combine (247Sports), in the Wizards' road blue with No. 18 (Wikipedia). He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn in the kit with the default skin tone. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
